Enumerates the principles of good supervision. Tells of a supervisor who knows the "book rules" for human relations but finds himself in trouble when trying to apply them to people on the job. Points out the things a man with supervisory responsibility needs to know about the way different people react to different situations, and the use he can make of this knowledge to improve his own job function and that of the people he supervises. Tells the story of a supervisor who tries to follow standard rules for getting the best from his people. He finds however, that his efforts at human relations backfire on him. Explains that through the discovery of his own and other people's 'INNER MAN,' he learns what he has been doing wrong and why.

Silver_Fleet_The.sy: The Silver Fleet was inspired by a true story from World War II. Holland now under German occupation, a Shipyard owner and Chief engineer Jaap van Leyden is summoned to build ships for the German war effort. The commission would allow Leyden to build sophisticated submarines whilst safeguarding jobs for the local Dutch workforce. A newly built U-boat, named U107 goes out on her first sea trial and is hijacked by a Dutch crew and they re-route the vessel to England. As such it provided an opportunity to refuel patriotism in the face of a seemingly interminable war and almost unbearable civilian hardship.

SocialCl1957.sy: Shows the differences in the life experience of three male babies from three different social classes. One young man succeeds his father as president of the family manufacturing company. Another, a middle-class white-collar worker at the same company, leaves the town of his birth and moves to New York City where he becomes a respected advertising art director, thus rising in social status. A third, born into the working class, trains as a mechanic and holds an influential job at a service station. The sociological tone of the film does not mask a sobering narrative of the limitations that social class divisions inflict on all Americans.

ansp-coll-1012_f16-0247.sy: This reel shows film footage from an Academy of Natural Sciences sponsored scientific expedition referred to as the 1928-1929 de Schauensee-Smith Asiatic Expedition to collect birds from Thailand, Singapore, and Myanmar. The film footage shows images of Thailand (historically known as Siam until 1939) including a local roadside market; motor vehicles crossing a small body of water; local Thai hunters with birds they’ve shot; packing birds for transport; river scenes including fishing; donkeys carrying supplies and equipment along a road; local women playing a wind instrument; members of the expedition party at camp; elephants and waterfalls. Two large species of birds shown in the film footage are the rufous-necked hornbill ( Aceros nipalensis ) and a sarus crane ( Antigone antigone ). Rodolphe Meyer de Schauensee, Curator of Ornithology, and collector, Lucas Bah are likely depicted in the film footage.
